instruction: Add CSRF protection using double-submit cookies with SameSite attributes. The system must validate tokens on state-changing requests, handle both form submissions and AJAX requests, and provide clear error messages.
reasoning: CSRF attacks trick authenticated users into making unintended requests. Double-submit cookies send token in cookie and header. SameSite prevents cross-site cookie sending. The system must work with forms and AJAX. Exemptions needed for safe methods and token-authenticated APIs. Clear errors help debugging.
answer: Server: generate CSRF token on session creation, set as cookie (_csrf) with SameSite=Strict, Secure, HttpOnly=false. Store hash in session. Client: read cookie, send in X-CSRF-Token header on POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH. Server: compare header token with cookie token using crypto.timingSafeEqual. Forms: include hidden field <input type='hidden' name='_csrf' value={token}>. Exemptions: GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, webhook endpoints (use signature verification), API endpoints with Bearer token auth. Error: return 403 with message 'CSRF validation failed. Please refresh the page and try again.' Log failures for security monitoring.

instruction: Implement focus management for a modal dialog that traps focus within the modal, handles keyboard navigation, and returns focus to the trigger element on close. The system must handle dynamic content and nested modals.
reasoning: Focus trapping keeps keyboard navigation within the modal. Tab cycles through focusable elements. Escape closes the modal. Focus returns to trigger element on close. instruction: Implement a multi-stage Docker build for a Node.js application that minimizes image size, separates build and runtime dependencies, and provides secure production images with non-root user.
reasoning: Multi-stage builds reduce image size by separating build and runtime. Build stage installs all dependencies and compiles. Runtime stage includes only production dependencies and built artifacts. Security: run as non-root user, use specific base image tags, minimize attack surface.
answer:
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build && npm prune --production

FROM node:20-alpine AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S nodejs && adduser -S nodejs -u 1001
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodejs:nodejs /app/package*.json ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodejs:nodejs /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodejs:nodejs /app/dist ./dist
USER nodejs
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 CMD wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]

instruction: Add a comprehensive CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions that runs tests, builds Docker images, deploys to staging automatically, and deploys to production with manual approval. The pipeline must provide fast feedback and reliable deployments.
reasoning: CI/CD automates testing and deployment. Tests run on every PR for fast feedback. Docker images build on merge to main. Staging deploys automatically for testing. Production deploys require approval for safety. The pipeline must handle failures gracefully and provide clear status.
answer:
name: CI/CD
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run type-check

  build:
    needs: test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - run: docker build -t ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }} .
      - run: docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }}

  deploy-staging:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    steps:
      - run: kubectl set image deployment/app app=ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }}

  deploy-production:
    needs: deploy-staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - run: kubectl set image deployment/app app=ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }}
